note: One expectation index per contract directory. Each case names the structural violations that prove its point as (pointer, keyword) pairs; a validator's free-text message is deliberately never recorded. The expected set must be a subset of what the validator reports, because a conditional rule often reports a broader violation alongside the specific one.

scan-mode-missing.proves: The authorised operating mode is mandatory. A run whose mode was never stated cannot later be argued to have been authorised for one, and there is deliberately no default.

scan-mode-unknown.proves: The mode vocabulary is closed at the two accepted modes. An invented, more aggressive-sounding mode is rejected by the contract before any component could act on it.

scan-mode-lowercase.proves: The vocabulary is case-sensitive, so a lowercased value cannot be matched against an accepted mode by accident.

target-url-not-http.proves: The target is an absolute http or https URL as a structural shape. This is a shape rule, not an egress or SSRF control: a value that validates here is still subject to whatever the scanner runtime enforces.

requested-at-offset.proves: Instants are UTC with the Z designator. A numeric offset is rejected by an explicit pattern rather than by a format annotation, which asserts nothing unless a checker is wired in.

contact-email-property.proves: The request carries opaque references, never personal data. The root is closed, so a contact address cannot be attached to a run request as a forward-compatible extension.
